name.text: Shared: Convert a large number to standard form

questiontext.text:
Write \[ {@number@} \] in standard form \[ a\times 10^n, \] where \[ 1 \leq a < 10. \]

Coefficient \(a\): [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

Exponent \(n\): [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]]

[[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

Move the decimal point until exactly one non-zero digit remains before it.

For \[ {@number@}, \] the coefficient is \[ {@coefficient_display@} \] and the decimal point moves \[ {@exponent@} \] places.

Therefore, \[ \boxed{ {@coefficient_display@} \times 10^{@exponent@} }. \]

Learners convert a large whole number to standard form using separate coefficient and exponent inputs.

Targets mathematically equivalent forms whose coefficient is outside the required standard-form interval.

Independent STACK implementation informed by the interaction pattern in Numbas NUMBAS-10751, "Scientific notation: large numbers to scientific notation", authored by Ben Brawn. No source wording or mathematical content is copied.

prtpartiallycorrect.text: One part is correct. Check the relationship between the coefficient and exponent.

prtincorrect.text: Remember that valid standard form requires the coefficient to be at least \(1\) but less than \(10\).

node.description: Coefficient is correct. Checks the exponent.

truefeedback.text: Correct. The coefficient is between \(1\) and \(10\), and the exponent matches the decimal-point movement.

falsefeedback.text: Your coefficient is correct. Recount how many places the decimal point moved.

node.description: Checks for an invalid coefficient that is ten times too large.

truefeedback.text:
Your expression has the correct numerical value, but it is not in standard form.

The coefficient must satisfy \[ 1 \leq a < 10. \] Move the decimal point one more place to the left and increase the exponent by \(1\).

falsefeedback.text: Check both the coefficient and exponent.

node.description: If the coefficient is incorrect for another reason, check whether the exponent is independently correct.

truefeedback.text: Your exponent is correct. Adjust the coefficient so it lies between \(1\) and \(10\).

falsefeedback.text: Recheck both parts of the standard form.

qtest.description: Correct coefficient and exponent receive full credit.
Equivalent value with invalid coefficient must receive zero credit.
Correct coefficient with wrong exponent receives half credit.
